title: Beyond the 956: Gerald Molen, Oscar-winning producer of 'Schindler's List' and 'Jurassic Park,' dies at 91
excerpt: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer behind Schindler's List and Jurassic Park, died Monday, November 23, 2026, at his home in Bigfork, Montana. He was 91.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer behind two of the most beloved films ever made — Schindler's List and Jurassic Park — has died at 91.

Molen died on Monday, November 23, 2026, at his longtime home in Bigfork, Montana, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced on social media. The Hollywood Reporter and Variety confirmed the news. No cause of death has been disclosed.

Born Gerald Robert Molen on January 6, 1935, in Great Falls, Montana, Molen moved with his family to North Hollywood in 1947. He began his long collaboration with director Steven Spielberg as the unit production manager on The Color Purple in 1985, and went on to serve as associate producer on *batteries not included in 1987 before becoming head of production at Spielberg's Amblin Entertainment.

His greatest achievement came with Schindler's List in 1993. The film won seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture, an honor Molen shared with Spielberg and fellow producer Branko Lustig. He also produced Rain Man, Hook, Jurassic Park, The Lost World: Jurassic Park, Twister, Casper and Minority Report.

Molen's films — from the dinosaurs of Jurassic Park to the history of Schindler's List — reached audiences around the world and remain among the most watched and honored movies ever made.

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter; Variety; ScreenRant.
